title: Alternating Series Bounds for Sin/Cos Taylor Series
description: Tighter remainder bounds for sin/cos Taylor series via the alternating series estimation theorem, improving on Lagrange bounds by factor (2N+1)

meta.author: Leibniz criterion (formalized in Lean 4)
originalContributions: sinTermAbs and cosTermAbs definitions for alternating series terms
Comparison theorem: alternating bound improves Lagrange by factor (2N+1)
Framework for applying alternating series estimation to Taylor series
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: sin/cos alternating remainder bounds. 3 sorries: term ratio formula, eventually decreasing, tendsto zero (all standard analysis, provable from Mathlib).

overview.historicalContext: The alternating series estimation theorem (Leibniz, 1682) gives tight error bounds for alternating series. Applied to sin/cos Taylor series, it improves the Lagrange remainder by exploiting the alternating sign structure.
overview.problemStatement: Show |sin(x) - S_N(x)| ≤ |x|^{2N+1}/(2N+1)! where S_N is the N-term partial sum of the sin Taylor series.
overview.text: Alternating series estimation gives tighter Taylor remainder bounds than Lagrange for sin/cos
overview.proofStrategy: Define term absolute values, verify they are eventually decreasing and tend to 0, apply the alternating series estimation theorem.
keyInsights: The alternating bound |x|^{2N+1}/(2N+1)! improves on Lagrange |x|^{2N+1}/(2N)! by a factor of (2N+1).
